newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Two suspected N.Korea infiltrators killed - Seoul.
newsitem.headline: Two suspected N.Korea infiltrators killed - Seoul.

text.p: Two men suspected to be North Korean infiltrators were shot dead on Tuesday by South Korean troops, a South Korean Defence Ministry spokesman said.
The two men, who exchanged fire with pursuing South Korean soldiers, were killed near the border with North Korea, he said. Several southern soldiers were wounded in the exchanges.
"We are not sure if the two killed today were from the submarine. Military investigators are looking into the matter," the spokesman said.
South Korean troops have been hunting for three missing North Koreans after a North Korean submarine landed 26 agents in September.

The Shark-class submarine ran aground off the eastern city of Kangnung on September 17 as it tried to pick up three spies it offloaded two days earlier, according to the only North Korean captured alive from the vessel.
Of the 26 North Koreans, 22 had earlier been shot dead after they fled into the surrounding hills.
The Defence Ministry spokesman said the two suspected infiltrators were shot dead at around 10.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) on Tuesday after they exchanged fire with southern troops.
"The two men suspected to be North Korean infiltrators were armed with M-16 rifles and hand grenades and exchanged fire with our soldiers on two different occasions," he said.
State radio said a South Korean colonel was killed and seven other soldiers were wounded during the firefight, but the spokesman could not confirm the report.
"Several soldiers on our side were wounded during the fighting but I don't have any further details," he said.

Rear Admiral Chales Moore, commander of the battle group of the U.S. aircraft carrier Independence, last week said South Korea faces the threat of sea-borne saboteurs but that the United States would send aircraft to defend it if war broke out on the Korean peninsula.
Tension has remained high on the peninsula, the world's last cold war frontier, since the North Korean submarine intruded into South Korea.
Tuesday's killing occurred as the United States and South Korea were holding a major military training exercise in and around Korea against any attack from the communist North.
The two-week exercise, called Foal Eagle '96, involves some 34,000 U.S. troops including 10,000 seamen from the U.S. Seventh Fleet, and most of South Korea's 655,000 military personnel.
